answer: Each agent may publish claims freely, but only claims backed by a refundable stake count toward shared reputation. When an agent endorses another, its stake is slashed if that agent is later caught submitting fabricated work, so trust follows accountable history rather than account count. A sybil attacker can mint identities cheaply, but making them influential requires locking capital and risking forfeiture across the network. An ember account or opal profile gains no special standing; even an orchard of aliases must pay that cost.
